prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family, small‑group, Medicare, Medicaid), whether you want in‑person help or are fine with virtual meetings, and what carriers/networks matter to you. I can help find highly rated brokers near you — tell me your ZIP code and what type of plan you’re shopping for — but meanwhile here are practical ways to find the best broker for your situation and what to look for:

How to find a good broker in Kansas City
- Decide the kind of help you need: individual/family ACA plan, small‑business group plan, Medicare (Part A/B/D/Medigap), or Medicaid/CHIP. Brokers often specialize.
- Use these directories:
  - National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent” tool
  - State insurance department license lookup: Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance (verify the agent is licensed)
  - Google/Yelp/BBB for local reviews and complaints
- Look for an independent broker (represents multiple carriers) rather than a captive agent tied to one insurer, unless you want a specific carrier.
- For Medicare, also consider your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) counselors — they provide unbiased, free counseling.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Are you licensed in Kansas and/or Missouri? (Kansas City straddles both states.)
- Do you represent multiple carriers or only one? Which ones?
- How are you paid? (Most are commission‑based; ask if any fees apply.)
- Will you help with enrollment and with claims or post‑enrollment problems?
- Can you show references or recent client reviews?
- Do you have experience with my specific needs (e.g., narrow‑network plans, anticipating high prescriptions, small‑business payroll integration, Medicare Special Needs Plans)?

What to check quickly (red flags)
- No state license or unwillingness to provide license number
- No references or online presence/reviews at all
- Pressure to pick a plan quickly or steer toward one carrier without explaining why

Local resources for Kansas City
- If you’re shopping during Open Enrollment for an ACA plan, you can also get free help from certified Marketplace navigators (search “healthcare.gov navigators Kansas City”).
- For Medicare, contact your state SHIP for free counseling.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code (or whether you’re on the Missouri or Kansas side of KC)
- Type of coverage you need (individual/family, small business, Medicare, etc.)
- Any priorities (doctors you must keep, budget, prescriptions)

I’ll find a short list of highly rated local brokers or navigators that fit your needs.
